text:
lee: FYI scheduling a short rolling maintenance for APAC-south1 tomorrow 14:00-14:30 UTC. Purpose: microcode sync (kernel + NIC) to address intermittent packet stalls on long-lived GPU streams. Target: cohort D (apac-saturn pools). Low-impact window, but want eyes.

ops-bot: Maintenance scheduled by lee: 2024-07-05T14:00:00Z -> 2024-07-05T14:30:00Z. Max concurrency = 3 nodes. Notifications enabled. :bell:

sumi: Does this touch Dedicated or Private installs? We have one private customer replicating in apac-south.

raf: Private control plane customers are out of scope. Dedicated pools are tagged reserved and excluded. We only touch scheduler-managed pools with tag cohort=D and schedulable=true.

lee: Plan summary: canary -> preheat KV + batchers -> drain nodes (graceful) -> apply microcode -> livecheck -> continue. If canary fails, rollback microcode and move traffic to us-east fallback pool.

sumi: Can we sequence by rack instead of arbitrary nodes? Last time cross-rack handoffs caused imbalanced backfill and extra cold KV hits.

raf: Good call. We'll operate rack-by-rack within cohort D. Each rack max 3 drains concurrently. Backfill will prefer warm standby nodes in the same AZ, then fall back cross-az to minimize cold cache misses.

lee: Preheat details: 8 priming jobs per pool, running our priming harness hitting /internal/priming with the week top prompt set. Will seed ~120k KV prefixes across racks. Preheat window = 12m before canary node drain.

sre-jen: Canary step: pick 2 low-traffic nodes (same rack) run the full flow, then 12m metrics window. Abort if any of: request-error >2% over 10m, token P95 > baseline+40ms for 10m, or packet-drop >0.7% sustained 10m. If abort -> immediate microcode revert + traffic steer to fallback pool.

ops-bot: Canary tags applied: canary=true. Will create incident channel if threshold breached.

tim: Cost note: if we spill to hosted standby we estimate ~4k credits extra for the window (worst-case), and tracing ingress ~15% spike due to priming churn. Ops budget notified.

customer-success: We'll send a brief customer notice to the two long-run jobs in apac-south and include the low-risk language. ETA to customers: 30m notice before start.

sumi: Networking check: previous NIC microcode touched Rx coalesce and we saw S3 retry storms because of a transient MTU mismatch. Can we validate ACLs and MTU compatibility?

raf: I already pulled the net diff. No ACL changes. We'll run an MTU sanity probe as part of preflight: ping -M do -s 1472 between node pairs and s3-proxy to validate. If failure -> hold.

lee: Runbook snippet:```bash
# preheat (example)
kubectl label nodes -l cohort=D preheat=true
python tools/priming/run_priming.py --region apac-south --pool saturn --parallel 8 --prompt-set weekly_top
# drain and upgrade
kubectl cordon node/apac-saturn-0$i
kubectl drain node/apac-saturn-0$i --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=90
ssh ops@apac-saturn-0$i 'sudo fwupd install microcode-2024-07-05.bin && sudo systemctl restart netdrv'
```

sre-jen: Add monitoring hooks: if packet-drop >0.5% for 10m -> trigger kernel fallback (ops: run rollback-script.sh) and reroute traffic to cohort E. Also add a tracing tag to priming jobs so we can filter those spikes out of production dashboards.

raf: I'll extend autoscaler pause to 45m for cohorts to avoid churn, and the backfill circuit will use prewarmed nodes only. We'll also throttle priming QPS to avoid overwhelming KV store.

ops-bot: @ena_sre added to oncall for the window. 10m reminder will be sent.

customer-success: Notified customers; included status page link and escalation path.

lee: Thanks. Oncall please be ready from 13:50 UTC. I'll post go/no-go 10m prior with final canary node IDs. Keep slack channel open for live updates. :rocket:
